newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mideast envoy Ross asked to stay on.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mideast envoy Ross asked to stay on.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross has been asked to stay on in the second Clinton administration which starts next week, Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Monday.

"Dennis Ross is truly a national asset to the United States, and keeping him as my advisor was one of the best decisions I made as secretary," Christopher, due to be succeeded next week by Madeleine Albright, said in a speech.
"It is great news that the President and Secretary-designate Albright have asked him to remain," he said in a luncheon address to the Conference of Presidents of Major Jewish Organisations.

Ross, a veteran of Middle East diplomacy, is currently in Israel trying to wind up the long-running Israeli-Palestinian negotiations on a partial Israeli troop withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.
Recently, Ross has been a subject of controversy. Some Palestinian officials have accused him of favouring Israel in the Hebron talks -- charges rejected by the State Department.

Last month, U.S. syndicated columnists Rowland Evans and Robert Novak said a move was afoot to shift Ross to a desk job in the State Department and have Richard Holbrooke, architect of the Bosnia peace accord, handle the negotiating. U.S. officials denied that report.

Christopher's remarks did not make clear whether Ross, who currently bears the title of Special Middle East Coordinator, would fulfil exactly the same role in the new administration, or for how long he would stay on.
